attributionOfTheCohortAFailures.finding: NOT attributable to the candidate-span change.
proof: All 9 Cohort A candidates are single-key (structuralNodeIds.length === 1), so R1's anchor-only rule yields the identical string the previous concatenation yielded. Measured per candidate in this run: anchorChars == preChangeChars for 9/9.
The compiler input is therefore byte-identical to the pre-change run; the only remaining variables are model nondeterminism and provider conditions.
R3 touches semantic-verification/verify.ts, which runs AFTER compilation and was not invoked by this runner at all, so it cannot have influenced these outcomes.

The two failures are the two slowest candidates in the pre-change baseline - 7.1 at 456 s and 7.1(b) at 393 s against a 480 s ceiling. Both were already marginal; 7.1 failed at 355 s and 7.1(b) reached the ceiling.
Zero operative-attribution violations and zero context-retention violations across the cohort.
attributionOfTheCohortAFailures.counterEvidenceConsidered: If the span change had broken something, the damage would be expected on DUAL-key candidates whose text actually changed - and none of those ran. A failure confined to byte-identical inputs is the signature of execution variance, not of a contract change.
